# Dr Tristan Hotham: data studies

> Dr Tristan Hotham, independent data-led researcher of politics, the past, platforms and places. Each study below pairs an interactive map with a write-up, and most have their data and paper archived on Zenodo with a DOI.

Author: Tristan Hotham, independent researcher. ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0003-4931-9349. Website: https://tristanhotham.com/. Blog: https://blog.tristanhotham.com/.

## How to cite

Cite the Zenodo record for a study: Hotham, T. (year). Title. Zenodo. https://doi.org/DOI
Example: Hotham, T. (2026). Bus Deserts: Villages Without a Usable Bus, the Last Bus Home and Who Lives Beyond the Network in England. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24116215

Each study page also shows a ready-made citation. Licences vary by study and are given in each Zenodo record and in studies.json.

## Machine-readable catalogue

- [studies.json](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/assets/studies.json): JSON feed of every study (r slug, t title, d one-line finding, theme, blog, data DOI, lic licence, kw keywords, year, ct full Zenodo title, tags detailed topic tags)
- [studies.csv](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/studies.csv): the same catalogue as CSV with citations
- [Catalogue page](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/catalogue/): static HTML with schema.org DataCatalog JSON-LD
- [Sitemap](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/sitemap.xml)
- [Corrections](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/corrections/): errors found in any study, what was wrong and what it now says

## Everyday life

- [Bus deserts](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/bus-deserts/): 41% of English villages have no usable weekday bus within 800 m, and 68% no Sunday bus nearby. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24116215 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Transport; Remoteness and access; Present day; England.
- [UFOs, big cats and Nessie](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ufos-cats-nessie/): What explains where people see them? UFO reports, police big cat records and the Loch Ness sightings register, tested. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24115201 Tags: Folklore; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Scotland; Data bias.
- [Who owns your street?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/overseas-owners/): Property in England and Wales held by overseas companies, by small area: 90,949 titles, 76% via Crown Dependencies and Overseas Territories. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24115197 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Housing; Present day; England; Wales; Place search.
- [How old is your neighbourhood?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/house-age/): The age of the homes in every small area of England and Wales: 21% predate 1919, and cities grow in rings. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24113859 Tags: Towns and cities; Buildings; Housing; Victorian; Present day; England; Wales; Place search.
- [Does anyone play your town?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/band-towns/): Every UK concert documented in MusicBrainz, 1960 to 2025, by council area: arena towns hold 10% of people but 53% of documented tour dates. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24113540 Tags: Music; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Place search.
- [Do the clocks kill?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/clock-change-crashes/): Road collisions in the week after the clocks change, Great Britain 1979 to 2025: no jump in spring or autumn across 9.1 million collisions. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24112856 Tags: Roads; Clocks and calendars; Seasons; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Before and after test.
- [Could Your Town Fit in Its Stadium?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/stadium-towns/): 190 sports grounds hold more people than their town: GCS Ballpark seats Sauget 42.5 times over, St Tiernach's Park seats Clones 15.4 times, and Turf Moor holds 27% of Burnley. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24087793 Tags: Towns and cities; Sport; Present day; Ireland; World; Place search; Data bias; Wikidata.
- [Not Where It Says on the Ticket](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/far-from-home/): 4,448 airports and 2,888 UK stations measured against the place in their name: Paris Vatry is 136 km from Paris, Frankfurt-Hahn 103 km, and Tiverton Parkway 9 km from Tiverton. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24087596 Tags: Place names; Railways; Transport; Present day; UK; World; Data bias; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [Shadows of the Giants](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/tower-shadows/): Winter sun at street level in eight UK city centres: on the shortest day the Shard's noon shadow is about 1.1 km long, and Canary Wharf's towers take 0.76 hours of sun from every square metre. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075302 Tags: Buildings; Sunlight; Present day; UK; London; OpenStreetMap.
- [Which Way Do Cricket Pitches Face?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/pitch-orientation/): Cricket strips in OpenStreetMap: 55% of the world's 1,394 run within 20 degrees of north to south, out of the low sun. Tennis follows the rule; football points anywhere. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075294 Tags: Sunlight; Sport; Present day; UK; World; OpenStreetMap.
- [Pilgrim Roads](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/pilgrim-roads/): 77,804 km of waymarked pilgrim routes: more than half lead to Santiago, and there is more of the Way of St James in Germany than in Spain. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23878607 Tags: Religion; Walking routes; Present day; Europe; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [After the Games](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/olympic-venues/): All 1,153 Olympic venues from Athens 1896 to Brisbane 2032: 88 served more than one Games, and where the sources say, 70% are still in use. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23878613 Tags: Heritage; Sport; Victorian; Twentieth century; Present day; World; Wikidata; Wikipedia.
- [The First Websites](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/first-websites/): From one server at CERN to 83 countries by 2000: 2,327 early websites mapped. The web began with physicists and was soon overwhelmingly American. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23878601 Tags: Internet; Science and technology; Twentieth century; Europe; World; Americas; Wikidata.
- [Every Tour de France, Mapped](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/tour-de-france/): Every stage since 1903: from one unbroken lap of France's edges to a race that hops, shorter and faster than ever. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873012 Tags: Sport; Twentieth century; Present day; Europe; Animated timeline; GeoNames.
- [Painted Places](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/painted-places/): Where landscape painters painted: the most painted place on Earth is a river, the Seine, and how far painters went from home. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873006 Tags: Rivers; Arts and culture; Long view; Europe; World; Wikidata.
- [Where Novels Are Set](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/novel-settings/): The real settings of 7,300 novels: London, New York and Paris dominate, and most authors stay close to where they were born. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23872996 Tags: Birthplaces; Arts and culture; Present day; London; World; Wikidata.
- [The AI Tapestry](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ai-tapestry/): The history of artificial intelligence stitched like the Bayeux Tapestry: from Ada Lovelace's engine to AI agents, with Latin captions, two winters, a comet called attention and a sourced note behind every scene. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23866753 Tags: Arts and culture; Science and technology; Victorian; Twentieth century; Present day; World.
- [Ghost Towns of the World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ghost-towns/): 5,448 abandoned settlements coloured by why they were left, and what open data does not record. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23857615 Tags: Lost places; Industry; Medieval; Twentieth century; World; Data bias; Classification; Wikidata; Wikipedia.
- [The World's Tallest Building](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/tallest-buildings/): Every record holder from the Great Pyramid to Jeddah Tower: Lincoln Cathedral held the title for 238 years, New York for 65. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23857607 Tags: Buildings; Long view; World; Data bias; Wikidata; Wikipedia.
- [Where Inventions Came From](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/inventions-map/): Where inventions came from over 3.3 million years: independent origins, the moving centre of invention, inventive cities and who gets the credit. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23856735 Tags: Science and technology; Long view; World; Data bias; Wikidata; Wikipedia.
- [Where the World's Music Comes From](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/music-birthplaces/): Birthplaces of 283,424 musicians and home towns of 29,489 bands: New York, London, Paris and Vienna lead, and Finland has the most metal bands per head. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23850286 Tags: Birthplaces; Women and gender; Music; Present day; World; Wikidata.
- [Where Every Film Was Shot](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/film-locations/): Filming locations of 23,468 films in Wikidata: Los Angeles, New York, London and Paris lead, Canada hosts the most foreign productions, and the Bond films reached 36 countries and territories. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23847353 Tags: Film and television; Present day; World; Americas; Wikidata.
- [Where Every Film Director Is From](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/director-birthplaces/): Birthplaces of 43,619 film directors: New York and Paris lead, Prague and Copenhagen lead per head, and women rose from 3% of new directors in the 1920s to 32% in the 2020s. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23847839 Tags: Birthplaces; Women and gender; Film and television; Twentieth century; Europe; World; Wikidata.
- [Who Was Big When?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/who-was-big-when/): 126 seasons of English league football on one map: crowds peaked at 41.2 million in 1948-49, the game moved south, and 39 towns have lost their league club. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23844506 Tags: Football; Sport; Victorian; Twentieth century; Present day; England; Wales; Animated timeline.
- [Where Football Clubs Come From](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/football-origins/): 45,931 clubs on an animated map from Sheffield FC in 1857: football spread by sea to Peru and Argentina before Hungary or Russia, and 1919 was the busiest founding year. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23844504 Tags: Football; Sport; Victorian; Twentieth century; World; Animated timeline; Wikidata.
- [Dinner, Tea or Supper?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/dinner-or-tea/): 12,522 dialect survey answers on what Britain calls its evening meal: tea in the north, dinner in the south, a tea line through the Midlands, and no sign of dinner moving north. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23842982 Tags: Dialect; Food and drink; Present day; UK; Dialect surveys.
- [What Does the World Drink?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/drinks-map/): 1,985 protected drink names, 32,425 wineries, breweries and distilleries and the national drink of 201 countries: the national drink is often tea. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23764738 Tags: Food and drink; Present day; World; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [What Does the World Eat?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/food-map/): National dishes for 186 countries, breakfasts for 73 and 2,706 regional dishes from fabada in Asturias to takoyaki in Osaka, and why there is no lunch map. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23761259 Tags: Clocks and calendars; Food and drink; Present day; World; Wikidata; Wikipedia.
- [Chips, Curry or Kebab?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/takeaways/): 62,949 takeaways and 141,306 restaurants on the food hygiene register sorted by what their names sell: the chip shop capital is the seaside, the curry capital Hounslow. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23748251 Tags: Business names; Food and drink; Present day; UK; Text mining; Classification; OpenStreetMap.
- [Signature Sports](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/niche-sports/): Which sport each country plays far more than the world, from 99,246 clubs: pesäpallo in Finland, tchoukball in Switzerland, hurling in Ireland, speedway in Poland. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23748255 Tags: Sport; Present day; UK; World; Location quotient; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [Born Here, Loved There](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/dog-breeds/): 573 dog breeds mapped to their countries of origin and set against kennel club registrations: in 8 of 10 countries the favourite dog was born somewhere else. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23748253 Tags: Public attention; Wildlife; Present day; World; Wikidata.
- [What Britain Drives](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/cars/): 42,728,066 MOT tests mapped by make, model and colour: the average British car is a blue Ford Fiesta, Scotland prefers white, and Shetland loves Toyotas. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23748249 Tags: Transport; Present day; UK; Scotland; Ireland.

## Early modern and modern

- [Booth's poverty map today](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/booth-today/): Are London's poorest streets of the 1890s still the poorest? Booth's colours read street by street against today's deprivation. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24115199 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Old maps; Victorian; Present day; London; Persistence test.
- [Crime in London, 1674 to 1913](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/old-bailey-crime/): The Old Bailey Proceedings mapped: from the gallows and transportation to prison, and where London's crimes happened. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24115191 Tags: Crime and punishment; Women and gender; Early modern; Georgian; Victorian; London.
- [Where slavery money came home](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/slavery-compensation/): 3,187 British addresses of slave-owners and claimants compensated in the 1830s: 36% in London. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24113857 Tags: Empire and colonialism; Poverty and wealth; Buildings; Georgian; UK; London.
- [A day from London](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/day-from-london/): How far a traveller leaving London at dawn could get in a day in 1750, the 1830s, 1850, 1910 and today: from about 5% of Great Britain's land to almost all of it. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24105504 Tags: Railways; Roads; Transport; Georgian; Victorian; Present day; UK; London.
- [Did Enclosure Cause the Swing Riots?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/enclosure-swing/): Every enclosure Act linked to 9,674 parishes in a pre-planned test: enclosed parishes rioted 2.7 points more in 1830, but no more than other parishes of the same size. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24091975 Tags: Protest and riots; Enclosure; Farming; Georgian; England; Chance test.
- [Fighting by Moonlight](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/battle-moons/): The Moon over 9,877 dated battles, with calendars corrected: they fall on every phase almost equally, and D-Day's bright Moon was the exception, not the rule. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24089703 Tags: Battles; Military history; Clocks and calendars; Space and astronomy; Long view; World; Wikidata.
- [Waterloo Road and the Clock in the Streets](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/battle-streets/): 1,690 UK streets named after battles from 1793 to 1944: 367 Waterloos and 340 Almas, and in 53 of 75 towns the later battles lie farther from the centre. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24086514 Tags: Battles; Commemoration; Street names; Georgian; Victorian; Twentieth century; UK; OpenStreetMap.
- [HMS Your Town](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ships-named/): 394 Royal Navy warships named after 135 British towns: Gloucester and Newcastle have had nine each, and the habit has come and gone for 350 years. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24052718 Tags: Military history; Naming; Ships and the sea; Long view; UK; Place search; Wikidata.
- [How Fast Did News Travel?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/news-speed/): Lincoln, Custer, the Titanic and Pearl Harbor in 936 American newspapers: dailies printed all but Custer the next day; the weekly press day was the real delay. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24052720 Tags: Science and technology; Victorian; Twentieth century; Americas; Text mining.
- [Saxton's Atlas, Measured](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/saxton-atlas/): 857 towns read on Saxton's maps of 1574 to 1579: a typical town is 1.4 km out, and north leans west by about 8 degrees, like a compass. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24052722 Tags: Old maps; Early modern; England; Wales; Map accuracy.
- [The Star Fort Belt](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/star-forts/): 1,307 bastioned forts drawn by their real outlines: the star fort did not creep out of Italy, it sailed, reaching India, Morocco and the Caribbean as early as Germany and England. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24043679 Tags: Empire and colonialism; Military history; Early modern; Europe; World; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [The Wealth of Nations, Mapped](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/gdp-through-time/): The world economy on one playable map from 10,000 BC to 2024: China and India made 45% of world output in 1820, 9% in 1950 and 30% today. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23899402 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Population; Long view; World; Asia; Animated timeline.
- [The Known World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/known-world/): 681 journeys from the Bronze Age to 1960 light up a dark world: Europe had recorded 20% of the land in 1492 and 67% by 1900, and much of the dark was known first to China, the Islamic world or Polynesian voyagers. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23897792 Tags: Exploration; Ships and the sea; Long view; World; Flow map.
- [How Close Did Ino Get?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ino-japan/): Ino Tadataka's 1821 survey of Japan's far north laid on today's coast: the drawn coastline sits a median 280 m from the modern line. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23882608 Tags: Old maps; Coasts and islands; Georgian; Asia; Map accuracy.
- [Transported](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/transported-convicts/): Every convict ship voyage to Australia, 1788 to 1868: the busiest port was Cork and the Second Fleet lost a quarter at sea. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873536 Tags: Crime and punishment; Empire and colonialism; Migration; Ships and the sea; Georgian; Victorian; UK; Ireland; Wikipedia.
- [Drowned Valleys](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/drowned-valleys/): The villages and valleys flooded for reservoirs, from Capel Celyn to Mologa, set against the great dam-building boom. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873532 Tags: Lost places; Rivers; Twentieth century; Wales; World; Wikidata; Wikipedia.
- [Fencing the Commons](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/enclosure/): Every parliamentary enclosure Act in England and Wales mapped place by place: two waves, and half passed in the wars with France. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873002 Tags: Parliament; Enclosure; Farming; Georgian; England; Wales.
- [Where the Asylums Were](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/asylums/): Britain's asylums mapped: most built between 1845 and 1914, almost none closed until the 1980s, and most closed sites are now homes. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873000 Tags: Health and disease; Buildings; Victorian; Twentieth century; UK; Wikipedia.
- [Ships Before Steam](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ships-before-steam/): Real ships' logbooks from 1750 to 1850 drawn as voyage lines: the trade winds, the volta do mar, the Brouwer route and how long voyages took. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23857609 Tags: Ships and the sea; Weather and climate; Georgian; World; Flow map.
- [Pirate Hotspots, Then and Now](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/piracy-hotspots/): 7,511 pirate attacks from 1993 to 2020, with IMB counts to 2026: piracy moved from the Strait of Malacca to Somalia, the Gulf of Guinea and now the Singapore Strait. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23856382 Tags: Crime and punishment; Ships and the sea; Twentieth century; Present day; Asia; Africa.
- [What's Left of the Workhouse?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/workhouses/): 356 traces of Britain and Ireland's workhouses in open data: surviving buildings, Workhouse Lanes and famine graves. 74% of survivors with a known later use became hospitals or homes. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23844516 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Buildings; Heritage; Victorian; UK; Ireland; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [Styles in Stone](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/architecture-styles/): 180,451 buildings with an architectural style, sorted into 25 families and mapped century by century: Romanesque gives way to Gothic, Baroque and the revivals, and Gothic Revival sails to Toronto and Melbourne. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23842988 Tags: Buildings; Heritage; Long view; Europe; World; Animated timeline; Classification; Wikidata.
- [The Listed Kingdom](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/listed-buildings/): All 465,740 entries on the UK's four lists of listed buildings on one map: mostly Georgian and Victorian houses, with a great many churches at the top. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23761428 Tags: Buildings; Heritage; Georgian; Victorian; UK; Text mining.
- [The Turnpike Towns](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/turnpike-towns/): England's 1,245 turnpike trusts and 10,927 surviving milestones and toll houses: did the towns on the turnpikes grow faster? Not that the data show. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729647 Tags: Towns and cities; Roads; Transport; Georgian; England; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [What’s the King on Your Postbox?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/postbox-kings/): The royal cypher on 61,435 UK post boxes: 3,614 still carry Victoria's VR and 143 Edward VIII's. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729632 Tags: Monarchy; Victorian; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Place search; OpenStreetMap.
- [The Lido Boom and Bust](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/lido-boom/): An open register of 73 British lidos: 33 of 49 dated openings came in the 1930s, and 14 closed pools have reopened. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729645 Tags: Heritage; Leisure; Sport; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; OpenStreetMap; Wikipedia.
- [Did the Pits Closing Still Show?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/pit-closures/): 167 of 196 deep mines closed between 1984 and 1994. Forty years on, pit towns have 2.0 points more adults long-term sick than similar towns. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729636 Tags: Health and disease; Poverty and wealth; Industry; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Persistence test; Census.
- [Bombs on Britain](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/air-raids/): All 61,542 civilians on the CWGC's Second World War roll for the UK, town by town: 51% died outside London. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729651 Tags: First World War; Military history; Second World War; Twentieth century; UK; London.
- [Ring the Changes](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ring-the-changes/): All 7,262 rings of change-ringing bells in Dove's Guide, mapped: jubilees, world wars and seven centuries of bell founding. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729640 Tags: Religion; Second World War; Music; Medieval; Long view; England.
- [How Many Names on Your War Memorial?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/war-memorials/): First World War names on 14,119 community memorials: 18.3 for every 1,000 people living there today, and only 36 small places record no dead. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23727150 Tags: Commemoration; First World War; Twentieth century; UK; Place search; Wikidata.
- [Did the Railway Invent the Seaside?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/seaside-railways/): Britain's resorts were already growing 1.6% a year before the railway came. The line brought a burst in its first decade. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23727126 Tags: Railways; Coasts and islands; Leisure; Victorian; UK; Before and after test; Census.
- [Captain Swing](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/captain-swing/): 3,117 Swing riot incidents of 1830: parishes with a threshing machine were twice as likely to riot, but 90% of riotous parishes had none. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23727132 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Protest and riots; Enclosure; Farming; Industry; Georgian; England; Chance test.
- [Britain’s Last Line of Defence](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/stop-lines/): 14,690 pillboxes and defences of 1940: the planned German landing beaches had 2.3 times the average density. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23727130 Tags: Military history; Second World War; Heritage; Coasts and islands; Twentieth century; UK.
- [Did Beeching Kill Your Town?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/beeching-cuts/): 3,331 stations closed from 1955 to 1975, and 643 towns lost every one. They are a little poorer and more car-bound today, but did not fall off a cliff. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23727113 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Railways; Transport; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Persistence test; Census.
- [Great Fires](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/great-fires/): 102 great town fires, 63% of them in the 1600s and 1700s: did the towns that burned rebuild bigger? Not clearly. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23691901 Tags: Towns and cities; Natural hazards; Early modern; Georgian; England; Persistence test; Wikipedia; Census.
- [Who Gets a Blue Plaque?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/blue-plaques/): 6,476 plaques across the UK and all 1,037 English Heritage plaques in London: 16% honour women, but 54% of those since 2020. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23691879 Tags: Commemoration; Famous people; Women and gender; Present day; UK; London; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [Rotten Boroughs: Where Are They Now?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/rotten-boroughs/): The 56 boroughs the 1832 Reform Act abolished, followed to today: 25 are villages, a hamlet or an empty hill. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23691899 Tags: Parliament; Lost places; Towns and cities; Georgian; Present day; England; Cornwall; Persistence test; Census.
- [Canal Mania](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/canal-mania/): Did England's canal towns boom, and do they still lead? Bigger today, not richer. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23689965 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Towns and cities; Transport; Georgian; Present day; England; Persistence test; Census.
- [Cholera 1849](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/cholera-1849/): Farr's elevation law, Snow's pump and whether London's worst-hit districts are still the poorest. - [Fire on the Hills](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/armada-beacons/): Could the Armada beacons carry the news? 193 beacon hills and the lines of sight between them. - [There and Back Again](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/there-and-back-again/): 43 great journeys from 600 BC to 1947, mapped and graded by the evidence that they happened. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23686755 Tags: Exploration; Long view; World; Data bias; Flow map; Wikipedia.
- [Cold Years, Witch Years?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/witch-hunts/): Scotland's 3,840 accused witches: did the panics follow cold years? They did not. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23677166 Tags: Crime and punishment; Weather and climate; Early modern; Scotland; Before and after test; Wikidata.
- [Whose Ships Sank Where?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/wrecks-of-europe/): 106,550 shipwrecks in Europe's seas, 1744 to 1945, by the flag they sailed under. - [Far From Home](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/victoria-cross/): Where each Victoria Cross was won, where its recipient was born, and the distance between. - [Thankful Villages: Luck or Size?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/thankful-villages/): The parishes where every man came home from the First World War. Small helps, but chance predicts hundreds more. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23676167 Tags: Commemoration; First World War; Twentieth century; England; Wales; Chance test.
- [Did Lighthouses Work?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/did-lighthouses-work/): Shipwrecks before and after the lights were lit on the British and Irish coast, 1700 to 1945. ## Romans to Tudors

- [Lost money](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/roman-coins/): Roman coins found in England, reign by reign: 275,206 Portable Antiquities Scheme records by district. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24115195 Tags: Coins and hoards; Metal detecting; Roman; England; Animated timeline; Portable Antiquities Scheme.
- [Where Romans wrote](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/roman-inscriptions/): 200,000 Latin inscriptions mapped across the Roman Empire: the epigraphic habit, ages on tombstones and soldiers far from home. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24114975 Tags: Military history; Languages; Roman; Europe; Data bias.
- [How accurate were old maps?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/map-accuracy/): Eight maps from Ptolemy to Ino Tadataka, re-fitted one way: median error from 26% of the mapped area on the Peutinger Table to under 2% on Ino's survey of Japan. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24104513 Tags: Old maps; Long view; World; Asia; Map accuracy.
- [Which Way Do the UK's Churches Face?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/church-orientation/): 32,007 church axes from OpenStreetMap: old churches face east, later ones follow the street, and the patron saint's sunrise makes no difference. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24052500 Tags: Religion; Sunlight; Medieval; Present day; UK; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [England in 1086, Drawn](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/domesday-world/): Every vill in Domesday Book on a hand-inked map: one house per household, a water wheel for every mill on its stream, 71,419 plough teams, and walled York, London and Winchester. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24045205 Tags: Domesday Book; Industry; Medieval; England; Hand-inked map.
- [How Accurate Were Portolan Charts?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/portolan-charts/): 349 places read on the Carta Pisana and the Catalan Atlas: both turned about 11 degrees off north, the Mediterranean within a few dozen kilometres, the Atlantic shrunk and misplaced. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24044644 Tags: Old maps; Ships and the sea; Medieval; Europe; Map accuracy.
- [Britain's Oldest Road Map, Measured](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/gough-map/): 157 towns found on a map of Britain drawn about 1360: a typical town is 18 km out of place and Wales is blown up, yet 72% of the miles written on its roads are within 25% of the real road. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24043677 Tags: Old maps; Roads; Medieval; UK; Wales; Map accuracy.
- [Caravanserais of the Silk Roads](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/caravanserais/): 960 caravanserais, khans and ribats on a hand-inked map: all together they crowd closer than a day's march, but the Safavid inns of Iran stand a median 34 km apart. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24043673 Tags: Roads; Transport; Medieval; Early modern; Asia; Hand-inked map; Clustering test; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [Al-Idrisi's World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/idrisi/): The map made for Roger II of Sicily in 1154, south at the top, measured on 431 towns: directions right to a median 10 degrees, and Sicily drawn best. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23882606 Tags: Old maps; Medieval; Europe; World; Map accuracy.
- [The Peutinger Table](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/peutinger/): A Roman road map 6.75 m long beside a modern one: it squashes the world 11 times north to south, yet most of its road distances are close to the real road. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23882604 Tags: Old maps; Roman roads; Roman; Europe; Map accuracy; Itiner-e.
- [Ptolemy's World, Measured](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ptolemy/): 2,358 of Ptolemy's places set against where they really are: shrink his longitudes by 0.72 and the map falls into place, but Scotland is turned on its side. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23882602 Tags: Old maps; Roman; Europe; World; Map accuracy; Pleiades.
- [The Hereford Mappa Mundi](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/mappa-mundi/): The largest surviving medieval world map set beside a modern one: its directions from Jerusalem are mostly right, but the Holy Land is drawn 4.5 times too big. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23878611 Tags: Religion; Old maps; Medieval; World; Map accuracy; Pleiades.
- [By Road and by Sea](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/roman-travel-times/): Fastest travel from Rome with ships as well as roads: Carthage was 210 days' walk by road and 6 with a ship, from Casson's ancient voyage speeds. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23863541 Tags: Roman roads; Ships and the sea; Transport; Roman; Europe; Africa; Pleiades; Itiner-e.
- [Roads of the Roman Empire](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/roman-roads/): 299,171 km of Roman road and a travel model: London was 81 days on foot from Rome, Constantinople 75 and Alexandria 180. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23857865 Tags: Roman roads; Roads; Transport; Roman; Europe; Africa; Itiner-e.
- [Holy Islands](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/holy-islands/): 20,228 European monasteries and hermitages checked against the shoreline: before 800, 4.3% stood on islands, from Skellig Michael to Iona; after 1100, about one in a hundred. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23844514 Tags: Religion; Monasteries; Coasts and islands; Early medieval; Medieval; Europe; Wikidata.
- [The Plague Years](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/plague-map/): 6,848 recorded plague years in 1,172 towns, 1347 to 1900: the Black Death's first wave, a return every 13 years or so, and the last outbreaks a century later in the Ottoman Mediterranean. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23844512 Tags: Health and disease; Plague; Medieval; Early modern; Europe; Animated timeline.
- [Britain in AD 500](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/britain-500/): What the ground can place instead of neat kingdoms: 891 pieces of evidence, a sharp east of graves and west of stones, and 24 kingdoms we can name but not draw. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23735819 Tags: Anglo-Saxons; Celtic; Archaeology; Hillforts; Early medieval; UK; Data bias.
- [Governing on the Move](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/royal-itineraries/): King John and Edward I mapped night by night: John moved on 42% of the days we can follow him, Edward on 23%. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729638 Tags: Government; Monarchy; Medieval; Early modern; England; Animated timeline; Text mining.
- [Market Towns That Failed](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/medieval-markets/): All 2,173 medieval market places in England and Wales, followed to today: 665 are towns, 1,168 villages, and a few are fields or sea. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23727143 Tags: Lost places; Plague; Towns and cities; Medieval; Present day; England; Wales; Persistence test.
- [From Domesday Mills to Modern Mills](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/domesday-mills/): 6,172 mills in Domesday Book: places that had one are 3.9 times as likely to have a watermill nearby today, but not a windmill. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23727139 Tags: Domesday Book; Industry; Rivers; Medieval; Present day; England; Persistence test; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [Minted](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/saxon-mints/): England's Anglo-Saxon and Norman mint towns from 70,995 coins: were they still the big towns in 1377, 1801 and today? DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23689961 Tags: Anglo-Saxons; Coins and hoards; Norman Conquest; Towns and cities; Early medieval; Medieval; England; Persistence test; Census.
- [The Roman Commuter Belt?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/roman-villas/): 617 Roman villas against today's household income: a premium that is almost all geography. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23689959 Tags: Poverty and wealth; Archaeology; Roman; Present day; England; Wales; Persistence test; Chance test.
- [Laid Waste: the Harrying of the North](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/harrying-of-the-north/): Where Domesday's 'waste' fell after 1069 to 1070, and how faint its scar is today. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23689579 Tags: Domesday Book; Norman Conquest; Medieval; Present day; Northern England; Persistence test.
- [The Conquest in Castles](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/norman-castles/): How fast Norman castles spread across Britain after Hastings, decade by decade. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23688583 Tags: Castles; Domesday Book; Norman Conquest; Medieval; UK; Wales; Animated timeline; Wikidata.
- [What Became of the Abbeys?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/after-the-abbeys/): 808 houses Henry VIII closed, traced to what stands on their sites today. - [Where Was the Battle?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/where-was-the-battle/): 88 proposed sites for 18 lost battles of early Britain, scored against the texts. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23677162 Tags: Battles; Archaeology; Roman; Early medieval; UK; Data bias; Wikidata.
- [The Villages That Vanished](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/lost-villages/): England's 2,222 deserted medieval villages against Domesday Book. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23677160 Tags: Domesday Book; Lost places; Plague; Enclosure; Medieval; England.
- [Is Domesday Destiny?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/domesday-destiny/): Does a place's size in 1086 still predict its size today? 13,000 Domesday places on one map. ## People and politics

- [Where party money lives](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/party-money/): Organisational donations to UK parties since 2001 by donor address: 59% from London, and a quarter from one constituency. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24113855 Tags: Political parties; Poverty and wealth; Present day; UK; London.
- [Two faces of the constituency](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/janus-places/): How often MPs name the places they represent: 42 times per 100 Facebook posts, 9 per 100 Commons speeches. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24105794 Tags: Parliament; Present day; UK; Text mining; Hansard.
- [What each constituency signs](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/petition-places/): Signatures by constituency for 734 UK Parliament petitions: every petition's map is clustered, and two broad signing profiles run through the seats. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24104517 Tags: Elections; Parliament; Present day; UK; Clustering test.
- [Roundhead or Cavalier, Leave or Remain?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/civil-war-leave/): Did the Danelaw or the Civil War leave a trace in the 2016 vote? Once demography is held equal, Danelaw seats voted much like the rest of England. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24104515 Tags: Brexit; Elections; Vikings and Norse; Early medieval; Early modern; Present day; England; Wales; Persistence test.
- [Which places get Parliament's attention?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/places-in-parliament/): A century of Commons mentions of 1,596 UK towns: London's share fell from 49% in the 1910s to 18% in the 2010s, and towns named in a seat's title get about twice the mentions. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24103126 Tags: Parliament; Public attention; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; London; Text mining; Hansard.
- [The Half-Life of Fame](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/fame-half-life/): 16,397 notable deaths on English Wikipedia: attention jumps about 15-fold in the month of a death and is back near its old level within two years. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24095451 Tags: Famous people; Public attention; Present day; World; Before and after test; Wikidata; Wikipedia.
- [Does Rain Keep Britain at Home?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/polling-rain/): Rain while the polls were open at 22 UK general elections since 1945: turnout about a tenth of a point lower per millimetre, but not established. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24094533 Tags: Elections; Weather and climate; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Chance test; Electoral results.
- [Does Parliament Notice Disasters, and Whose?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/disaster-attention/): 64 UK disasters, 1910 to 2020: the Commons names the place about 10 times as often in the month of a disaster, and most of that fades within the year. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24094465 Tags: Parliament; Public attention; Natural hazards; Twentieth century; UK; Before and after test; Hansard.
- [Twinned with Europe, Voted Remain?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/twins-remain/): 1,445 British town twinnings against the 2016 vote: places twinned with Europe voted about the same as similar places. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24094354 Tags: Brexit; Elections; Town twinning; Present day; UK; Europe; Chance test; Wikidata.
- [Do By-elections Make Parliament Listen?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/byelection-attention/): 366 UK by-elections and a century of Hansard: the town gets about four times the Commons mentions around polling day, and more for two years. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24094209 Tags: Elections; Parliament; Public attention; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Before and after test; Hansard.
- [Gladstone Road or Disraeli Street?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/pm-streets/): Every Victorian statesman's street in Britain, set against how 160 towns voted, 1868 to 1900: Liberal names everywhere, a little more in Liberal towns. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24092656 Tags: Commemoration; Elections; Political parties; Street names; Victorian; UK; OpenStreetMap.
- [Who gets talked about?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/wiki-vs-hansard/): Wikipedia reading against Commons debate for 1,425 UK towns: a seat named after a place goes with 2.2 times the mentions. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24092582 Tags: Parliament; Public attention; Present day; UK; Text mining; Wikipedia; Hansard.
- [Does a Local MP Get a Local Bonus?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/local-mp-bonus/): 31,737 MP returns since 1832: MPs born within 25 km of their seat win about 1.3 points more of the vote, but are defeated just as often. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24092360 Tags: Birthplaces; Elections; Parliament; Georgian; Victorian; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Electoral results.
- [The War Dead and the Rise of Labour](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/war-dead-labour/): First World War memorial names against every election from 1906 to 1924: places that lost more men swung less to Labour in 1918, not more. A suggestive, pre-planned test. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24092043 Tags: Elections; First World War; Political parties; Twentieth century; UK; Electoral results.
- [Did Beeching's Cuts Make Places Vote Leave?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/beeching-leave/): 3,206 stations closed from 1955 to 1975. Seats that lost more voted Leave more, but compared with similar seats the link vanishes: a well-powered null. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24091897 Tags: Brexit; Elections; Railways; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Chance test.
- [The Renamed World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/renamed-world/): 6,842 official renamings of places in Wikidata, by decade and by why: revolution, its undoing, war and nation-building. The busiest year was Romania's 1964. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075300 Tags: Naming; Place names; Twentieth century; World; Animated timeline; Classification; Wikidata.
- [Every Embassy in the World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/embassies/): 15,584 embassies, consulates and missions from open data: Washington hosts 181 embassies, the Holy See runs 88 nunciatures, and the diplomatic web traced from the Amarna letters to today. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23899268 Tags: Government; Present day; World; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.
- [When Did Your Country Lose 11 Days?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/calendar-switch/): The Gregorian calendar, driving side, metric units and votes for women, switched country by country. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873008 Tags: Government; Women and gender; Clocks and calendars; Early modern; Twentieth century; World; Animated timeline; Place search; Wikipedia.
- [The Largest City on Earth](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/largest-cities/): Six thousand years of the world's biggest city, from Uruk to Jakarta, and how the centre of the urban world wandered. - [How the World Is Governed](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/government-types/): 197 systems of government compared on eight features: 12 families, 112 exact systems, and 80 countries with a system no one else shares. - [Where the Borders Are Straight](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/straight-borders/): 19% of the world's land borders are ruler-straight and Africa holds over half of that length, but North America is straighter by share. - [Capitals That Moved](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/moving-capitals/): 184 capital moves since 1500, checked by hand. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23847841 Tags: Government; Towns and cities; Early modern; Long view; World; Checked by hand; Wikidata.
- [Who Held the Map?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/flags-through-time/): Twelve centuries of the world map, 800 to 2010, each piece of land filled with the flag of whoever held it. In 1000 no land can honestly be shown with a flag; by 2010, 97% can. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23845994 Tags: Borders; Empire and colonialism; Long view; World; Animated timeline; Wikidata.
- [Where Languages Come From](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/language-origins/): Every one of 7,674 spoken languages with its family tree, endangerment and speakers, plus the proposed homelands of the great families: 421 separate lineages, and 52.1% of languages endangered. - [Born and Bred? How Local Are MPs?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/mp-localness/): Where 10,094 MPs since 1832 were born, set against the seats they won: for 170 years about a quarter were born in their seat's county, and since 2010 it is 41.9%. ## Land, sea and sky

- [Can you see the sea?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/sea-view/): Sight lines from every 1 km square of the UK: 26% of the land has a sea view from the ground. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24106075 Tags: Coasts and islands; Hills and mountains; Present day; UK; Line of sight; Terrain model.
- [The trig pillar network](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/trig-network/): How Britain was measured: 6,573 OS trig pillars, and 95% of the lines between neighbouring primary stations still clear on a terrain model. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24104643 Tags: Heritage; Hills and mountains; Present day; UK; Line of sight; Terrain model; Ordnance Survey.
- [Where the lifeboats go](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/lifeboat-launches/): Five years of RNLI launches mapped: half go less than 4.5 km from the station, and all-weather boats go about two and a half times further than inshore boats. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24104519 Tags: Ships and the sea; Coasts and islands; Seasons; Present day; UK.
- [Where the Sun Sets into the Sea](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/sea-sunsets/): 1,717 beaches in Britain and Ireland, day by day: 47% see a sunset into open sea on some day of the year, only 52 every day, and Arran hides 134 sunsets a year from Troon. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24089891 Tags: Coasts and islands; Sunlight; Present day; UK; Ireland; Line of sight; OpenStreetMap.
- [Manhattanhenge for Every British Town](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/street-henge/): The days the sun rises or sets straight down 37,224 streets in 377 UK towns: 1,072 line up with a solstice, about as many as chance, and Midsummer Boulevard misses midsummer. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075296 Tags: Street names; Sunlight; Present day; UK; Terrain model; OpenStreetMap.
- [Britain's Sunless Valleys](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/sunless-valleys/): Skylines for 36,692 UK settlements: 64 get no direct sun on the winter solstice, and Camas-luinie goes 123 days without it. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24055579 Tags: Hills and mountains; Sunlight; Present day; UK; Scotland; Wales; Terrain model; Satellite and lidar.
- [Where the Storks Go](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/bird-migration/): 228 tagged birds across three continents: young storks fly 0.6% of their distance over the sea and squeeze through Gibraltar and the Bosporus, while ospreys and cuckoos cross open water. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24043675 Tags: Migration; Wildlife; Present day; Europe; World; Africa; Flow map.
- [When the Ice Came South](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ice-ages/): The Northern Hemisphere's ice sheets at 18 moments of the last 3.6 million years. The last ice age was only the fourth largest. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23878609 Tags: Ice ages and sea level; Deep time; Prehistory; World; Animated timeline.
- [London's Buried Rivers](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/buried-rivers/): What still flows in the open and what runs in the dark: the Tyburn, Westbourne and Fleet are almost wholly underground. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873534 Tags: Lost places; Rivers; Present day; London; OpenStreetMap.
- [Every Tsunami on Record](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/tsunamis/): Every recorded tsunami since 1610 BC and the places its water reached: most start with an earthquake, the highest ran 524 m uphill. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873530 Tags: Coasts and islands; Geology; Natural hazards; Long view; World.
- [The Middle of Nowhere](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/remote-places/): How far every point on land is from the nearest town: a quarter of the land outside Antarctica is more than 100 km from one. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23873014 Tags: Remoteness and access; Present day; World; Natural Earth; GeoNames.
- [Junk on the Moon and Mars](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/moon-mars/): Every human-made object on two worlds: 133 on the Moon and 27 on Mars, from landers and rovers to golf balls. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23872994 Tags: Exploration; Heritage; Space and astronomy; Twentieth century; Present day; Beyond Earth; Wikipedia.
- [A Lidar Map of the World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/lidar-world/): Fifteen national lidar surveys in one zoomable map: the ground with the trees and buildings taken away. Hillforts in forests, the craters of Verdun and Messines, Roman gold mines and Japan's largest burial mound. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23866755 Tags: Archaeology; Hillforts; Hills and mountains; Present day; World; Terrain model; Satellite and lidar.
- [A Tolkien-Style Map of the Whole World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ink-map/): The whole Earth drawn like a hand-inked fantasy map: peaks only on real high ground, dunes for deserts, castles, town walls and great landmarks in pictures, rivers and beaches named in blue, and towns of tiny red and blue roofed houses packed tightest at the centre. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23860252 Tags: Hills and mountains; Present day; World; Hand-inked map; Terrain model; OpenStreetMap.
- [Every Storm Since 1851](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/hurricane-tracks/): Every hurricane, typhoon and cyclone in the global best-track archive: where storms form and hit, and the rising share reaching Category 4 or 5 since 1980. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23858050 Tags: Natural hazards; Weather and climate; Victorian; Twentieth century; Present day; World; Data bias.
- [The Earth at Night](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/earth-at-night/): Satellite night lights 2012 to 2024: 57% more light, Nepal up ninefold, Ukraine and Yemen half dark, and why LEDs fool the satellite. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23857867 Tags: Light pollution; Present day; World; Animated timeline; Satellite and lidar.
- [Lighthouses of the World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/lighthouses/): 9,770 lighthouses on one glowing map: lights per km of coast, when they were built, the oldest still standing and the tallest. - [Every Rocket Launch Since Sputnik](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/rocket-launches/): 7,416 orbital launches since 1957: the space race, the record 329 of 2025, the busiest spaceports and the Point Nemo spacecraft cemetery. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23857611 Tags: Space and astronomy; Science and technology; Twentieth century; Present day; World; Animated timeline.
- [Lost at Sea](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/lost-at-sea/): 472 famous disappearances at sea tested against shipping traffic: the Bermuda Triangle is no worse than its neighbours. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23856867 Tags: Ships and the sea; Shipwrecks; Long view; World; Americas; Chance test; Wikipedia.
- [The Internet's Seabed](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/submarine-cables/): Every submarine internet cable: when each was laid, who owns them, and the straits and hubs where they crowd together. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23856606 Tags: Oceans; Internet; Science and technology; Present day; World.
- [How Deep Is the Sea?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ocean-depth/): The whole ocean floor in depth: the average sea floor lies 3,675 m down, 74% of it is abyssal, and only 28.7% is mapped to modern standards. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23850290 Tags: Hills and mountains; Oceans; Present day; World; Data bias; Terrain model.
- [Shipwrecks of the World, and How Many over Time](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/world-shipwrecks/): 243,071 wrecks listed on Wikipedia since 1700, year by year: three of the five worst years are war years, with 1944 the worst of all. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23850288 Tags: Second World War; Ships and the sea; Shipwrecks; Georgian; Twentieth century; World; Animated timeline; Wikipedia.
- [How High Is the World?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/world-terrain/): The height of the whole planet on one map: the land averages 807 m, only 11% of it is above 2,000 m, and only 1.9% of city dwellers live that high. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23848929 Tags: Hills and mountains; Present day; World; Terrain model; Wikidata; Satellite and lidar.
- [Where the World's Islands Are](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/world-islands/): 181,588 islands in a detailed open shoreline map, 23,150 over a square kilometre. Canada has the most, and 10.3% of the world's people live on one. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23848300 Tags: Coasts and islands; Population; Present day; World; Natural Earth.
- [Who Shares the World's Rivers?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/shared-rivers/): 313 river basins cross a border, draining 47% of the land outside Antarctica and holding 45% of the world's people. Plus the great rivers measured on one map. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23848925 Tags: Borders; Rivers; Present day; World; Natural Earth.
- [In the Shadow of the Volcano](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/volcano-neighbours/): All 1,215 Holocene volcanoes and their neighbours: at least 147 million people live within 30 km of one, and 76 volcanoes have a million or more. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23847549 Tags: Geology; Natural hazards; Population; Present day; World; Data bias.
- [Where Space Rocks Land](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/meteorite-falls/): 45,715 meteorites: 65% found on Antarctic ice and 24% in hot deserts, while the 1,107 seen to fall follow people, not the sky. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23847547 Tags: Geology; Space and astronomy; Present day; World; Data bias.
- [Desert, Forest, Ice](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/land-cover-1900/): The world's land in 1900 and now: farms covered 19% of the ice-free land in 1900 and cover 37% today. Where the new fields came from, and where trees came back. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23847970 Tags: Farming; Land use; Trees and woodland; Victorian; Present day; World.
- [Where the Wind Blows](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/wind-map/): The world's winds month by month, from the trade winds to the Roaring Forties, and 5,344 wind farms: 82% of onshore capacity stands on ground windier than its country's median. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23844510 Tags: Seasons; Weather and climate; Present day; UK; World; Animated timeline; WorldClim.
- [Where the Animals Are](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/livestock-map/): 35.3 billion farm animals mapped every 10 km and counted since 1961: chickens have multiplied 7.1 times, and farm mammals outnumber people in 40 countries. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23842984 Tags: Farming; Wildlife; Twentieth century; Present day; World; FAOSTAT.
- [What the World Grows](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/crop-map/): The leading crop on every 10 km square of the world's farmland, and sixty years of change: half the harvest of 34 crops grows on 6.4% of the world's land. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23842986 Tags: Farming; Land use; Twentieth century; Present day; World; FAOSTAT.
- [Signature Species](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/county-wildlife/): 60.9 million open wildlife records sorted into 118 vice counties, to find the species each one records far more often than the rest of Britain and Northern Ireland. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23761434 Tags: Wildlife; Present day; UK; Ireland; Data bias; Location quotient.
- [Darkest Skies](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/dark-skies/): The glow of the world's lights modelled from satellite images and checked against 6,653 sky meter readings: 52% of people, and 85% in the UK, cannot see the Milky Way from home. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23757707 Tags: Light pollution; Present day; UK; World; Satellite and lidar.
- [Where Rain Goes](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/where-rain-goes/): Every place in Britain, Ireland and the world followed downhill to the sea: 50% of Great Britain drains to the North Sea, and 24% of the world's land never reaches the sea at all. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23757699 Tags: Rivers; Weather and climate; Present day; UK; Ireland; World; Terrain model; Ordnance Survey.
- [How Wrong Is Your Clock?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/clock-vs-sun/): For 76% of the world's people the clock runs ahead of the sun: the gap everywhere, and why winter mornings in Galicia stay dark until after nine. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23757705 Tags: Clocks and calendars; Sunlight; Present day; Atlantic Europe; World; Asia; Place search.
- [What Grows Where](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/tree-map/): Every wood in Great Britain by type, England's public forests by species and planting year, and 88 tree genera worldwide: woodland covers 13.7% of Great Britain, 19.1% of Scotland but 10.3% of England. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23739844 Tags: Land use; Trees and woodland; Wildlife; Present day; UK; England; Data bias; GBIF.
- [Hard Water](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/hard-water/): Water hardness from 16,682 river, lake and groundwater stations, and a simple model that guesses it from the rocks: Scandinavia's median is 14 mg/l, the Yucatán's 514. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23735823 Tags: Geology; Rivers; Present day; UK; Ireland; World.
- [The Footpath Capital](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/footpaths/): Every council in England and Wales by miles of public footpath per square mile: Rossendale tops it at 7.7, and the South Pennine mill towns fill the top ten. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23736297 Tags: Remoteness and access; Walking routes; Present day; England; Wales; OpenStreetMap.
- [The Rocks Beneath](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/rocks-beneath/): A geological map of the British Isles and the world in the colours of 1969: Carboniferous rocks cover 17.5% of Great Britain, and England's layers get younger all the way to London. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23734961 Tags: Geology; Deep time; UK; Ireland; World.
- [Drowned and Rising](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/sea-level/): A bathtub model of every sea level from the Ice Age to an ice-free world: Britain becomes an island at −30 m, and at +70 m a third of the UK is under water. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23732577 Tags: Coasts and islands; Ice ages and sea level; Deep time; Prehistory; Present day; UK; World; Terrain model.
- [How Many Months Are Pleasantly Warm?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/pleasant-months/): Months with afternoon highs of 18 to 27 °C: the average city dweller gets 3.6 a year now and 2.9 by 2041 to 2060. Pick your own band. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23732575 Tags: Towns and cities; Seasons; Weather and climate; Present day; World; WorldClim.
- [Sun and Rain: the World](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/sun-and-rain/): The world's sunshine against its rainfall: only 3% of land is both sunny and wet, and 84% is sunnier than anywhere in the UK. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23732579 Tags: Sunlight; Weather and climate; Present day; UK; World; Bivariate map; WorldClim.
- [Sun and Rain: the UK](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/sun-and-rain-uk/): Every square kilometre of the UK by sunshine and rainfall at once. Since 1961 to 1990 the country has become 5.6% sunnier and 7.2% wetter. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23732581 Tags: Sunlight; Weather and climate; Twentieth century; Present day; UK; Bivariate map.
- [When Did Your Town Last See a Total Eclipse?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/eclipse-towns/): Every path of totality across Britain and Ireland from AD 1000 to 2200, tested for 17,103 places: for most towns the last was in 1715 or 1724. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729634 Tags: Space and astronomy; Sunlight; Long view; UK; Ireland; Place search.
- [Britain’s Earthquakes Since 1382](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/british-earthquakes/): All 7,032 quakes in the BGS catalogues: a magnitude 4 about every 3 years, and the busiest modern zones were coalfields. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729642 Tags: Industry; Geology; Natural hazards; Medieval; Long view; UK; Data bias.
- [Where Are Britain’s Oldest Trees?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ancient-trees/): 1,626 notable trees on OpenStreetMap: oaks dominate, yews hug the old churches, and giants stand in the royal forests. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23729649 Tags: Monarchy; Religion; Trees and woodland; Present day; UK; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata.

## Names on the map

- [Does the 1974 border still show?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/rose-border/): Lancashire and Yorkshire in business names: where the old line did not move, it is still sharp, and the Lancashire name thins out in Greater Manchester and Merseyside. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24104646 Tags: Borders; Business names; Twentieth century; Present day; Northern England; Persistence test; OpenStreetMap.
- [Lost kingdoms on the high street](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/lost-kingdoms/): Businesses named after Wessex, Mercia and Northumbria still cluster inside the old kingdoms: 75 of 95 Wessex names are in Wessex. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24104339 Tags: Anglo-Saxons; Business names; Early medieval; Present day; England; Northern England; Persistence test; OpenStreetMap.
- [Ginnel, Snicket or Twitten?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/alleyway-words/): 3,382 named alleys on UK street signs by their word: 88% of twittens are in Sussex, every chare is in the North East, and London's 375 named alleys use a regional word just twice. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24086512 Tags: Dialect; Street names; Present day; UK; Scotland; Text mining; OpenStreetMap.
- [Who Named Antarctica?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/antarctica-names/): 20,151 Antarctic place names by who named them, when and after whom: the US named 26% and the UK 20%, and only 3.4% of the people honoured are women. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075308 Tags: Commemoration; Women and gender; Naming; Place names; Twentieth century; World; Wikidata.
- [Who's on the Mountains?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/mountain-names/): 2,228 mountains named after people, linked to where those people were born: 84% of the person-named peaks of Australia and New Zealand honour someone born on another continent. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075304 Tags: Birthplaces; Commemoration; Empire and colonialism; Naming; Place names; Hills and mountains; Present day; World; Wikidata.
- [Where the Wolves Were](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/animal-place-names/): 662 places in Britain and Ireland named after animals, checked by hand: wolf names sit high in the hills, at a median 256 m against 103 m for similar names. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24075292 Tags: Anglo-Saxons; Languages; Place names; Wildlife; Early medieval; UK; Ireland; Checked by hand; OpenStreetMap.
- [Avon Means River](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/river-names/): 32,068 named UK rivers and streams: 37 of England's 60 biggest rivers kept names older than English, and the Norse beck still marks where Vikings settled. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24063208 Tags: Celtic; Languages; Place names; Vikings and Norse; Rivers; Early medieval; UK; OpenStreetMap.
- [Named for a Place, Living Somewhere Else?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/species-places/): 2,901 species named after places, tested against GBIF records: 98% are recorded in their namesake's country, but the coco de mer, named for the Maldives, grows in the Seychelles. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24058122 Tags: Naming; Place names; Wildlife; Present day; World; Wikidata; GBIF.
- [Towns with an Asteroid](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/asteroid-towns/): 2,193 asteroids named after places on Earth, each linked to the observatory that found it: Japan has the most, Finland the most per head. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24052724 Tags: Naming; Place names; Space and astronomy; Present day; World; Asia; Wikidata.
- [Who's on the Moon?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/moon-names/): The Earth birthplaces of the 2,718 people with features on the Moon, Mercury, Venus and Mars: 75% of the Moon's were born in Europe. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24055577 Tags: Birthplaces; Commemoration; Naming; Space and astronomy; Present day; Beyond Earth; Wikidata.
- [The Colours of the World's Place Names](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/colour-names/): 138,453 places named black, white, red, green, blue or yellow in 20 languages: rivers run black, springs run white, and Cerro Colorado is the commonest colour name on Earth. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24043681 Tags: Languages; Place names; Rivers; Present day; World; Text mining; GeoNames.
- [Named After Somewhere Else](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/named-after/): 3,981 places named after another place: most names come from a river or the town next door, 14% crossed an ocean, and Britain gave away the most. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23878605 Tags: Empire and colonialism; Migration; Naming; Place names; Long view; UK; World; Flow map; Wikidata.
- [The World's Strangest Borders](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/border-oddities/): Every enclave, exclave and tripoint: 42 true enclaves in 85 pieces, and a front door split between two countries. - [Has Your Surname Left Home?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/surname-birthplaces/): Where 133,761 notable Britons with each surname were born, 1800s against since 1950: Welsh Joneses and Cornish Tre- names are leaving home, though slowly. - [Bloody Place Names](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/bloody-place-names/): 756 grim names on the OS map against 507 battles: only the Battles mark battlefields. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23677164 Tags: Battles; Place names; Long view; UK; Chance test; Wikidata; Ordnance Survey.
- [What Pub Names Remember](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/pub-sign-history/): Every named pub in Britain, grouped and mapped: Red Lions, Royal Oaks and the names that give a county away. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23676494 Tags: Monarchy; Business names; Food and drink; Present day; UK; Classification; OpenStreetMap.
- [The Geography of Saints](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/saints-geography/): 17,116 church dedications mapped: Andrew in Scotland, David in Wales, and 98 saints found only in Cornwall. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23676496 Tags: Religion; Celtic; Medieval; UK; Scotland; Wales; Cornwall; OpenStreetMap.
- [Is There a Barrow in Barrow?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/barrow-in-barrow/): Do places named from Old English beorg sit by burial mounds? 129 names against 6,100 scheduled barrows. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23676161 Tags: Anglo-Saxons; Place names; Barrows; Prehistory; Early medieval; England.
- [Dale, Down, Fell and Beck](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/dale-down-fell-beck/): Walk north and the water changes its name. The words Britain uses for hills, valleys and streams, mapped. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23674173 Tags: Dialect; Place names; Vikings and Norse; Hills and mountains; Rivers; Early medieval; UK; Northern England; Ordnance Survey.
- [The High Ones](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/the-high-ones/): The Brigantes, Brigantium and the Celtic word for high, traced across Europe. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24109742 Tags: Celtic; Languages; Place names; Roman; Europe; Atlantic Europe; GeoNames; Pleiades.

## Prehistory and monuments

- [Ancient DNA on the Map](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ancient-dna/): 16,496 ancient genomes placed where and when they lived: the first farmers spread out of Anatolia at about a kilometre a year. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23872992 Tags: Migration; Archaeology; Prehistory; Europe; Asia; Data bias.
- [Life on the Moving Map](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/deep-time-life/): 540 million years of drifting continents, from Pangaea onwards, with fossil animals from trilobites to dinosaurs where they lived. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23856869 Tags: Geology; Wildlife; Deep time; World; Animated timeline; Data bias.
- [Ley Lines, Tested](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/ley-lines/): 50,822 churches, barrows, stones, hillforts and wells against random points: crowding, not planning, explains the leys. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23691884 Tags: Religion; Folklore; Hillforts; Megaliths; Prehistory; UK; Chance test; Clustering test; OpenStreetMap.
- [Did Fairy Belief Protect Ireland’s Ringforts?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/fairy-forts/): 31,431 ringforts set against barrows, enclosures and moated sites: the fairies left few fingerprints. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23691873 Tags: Folklore; Archaeology; Monuments; Prehistory; Medieval; Ireland; Ordnance Survey.
- [Still Standing](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/oldest-buildings/): 6,837 buildings from before AD 1100 on one map, and what kept them standing. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23687611 Tags: Religion; Buildings; Heritage; Roman; Early medieval; Europe; World; Wikidata.
- [Same Shape, Different Millennia](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/stone-circles/): Every stone circle in Europe's open data, sorted into traditions and dated. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23685255 Tags: Megaliths; Monuments; Prehistory; Europe; Classification; OpenStreetMap; Wikidata; Radiocarbon dates.
- [Is the Barrow a European Thing?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/barrows-of-europe/): 99,049 burial mounds from Ireland to the steppe, with radiocarbon dates. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23685257 Tags: Barrows; Monuments; Prehistory; Ireland; Europe; Data bias; OpenStreetMap; Radiocarbon dates.
- [The Megalith Highway](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/megalith-highway/): 13,280 megalithic monuments: did the idea of the great stone tomb travel by sea? DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23685253 Tags: Archaeology; Megaliths; Monuments; Prehistory; Atlantic Europe; OpenStreetMap; Radiocarbon dates.
- [Within Sight](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/within-sight/): Could Britain and Ireland's 4,147 hillforts see each other? A line-of-sight network across two islands. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23674175 Tags: Hillforts; Prehistory; UK; Ireland; Line of sight; Chance test; Terrain model.
- [The Famous Few](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/famous-few/): 4,147 hillforts, ten years of Wikipedia reading. Eleven sites take half of it, mostly for their castles. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23649935 Tags: Famous people; Public attention; Hillforts; Prehistory; Present day; UK; Ireland; Wikipedia.
- [Rings in the Rock](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/rings-in-the-rock/): Cup-and-ring carvings on Europe's Atlantic edge: where they are, when, and what they might mean. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24110050 Tags: Archaeology; Arts and culture; Prehistory; Scotland; Europe; Atlantic Europe.
- [The Triskell Boom](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/triskell-boom/): How an ancient triple spiral became a modern Celtic badge, 3500 BC to today. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24110205 Tags: Celtic; Arts and culture; Prehistory; Present day; Atlantic Europe; Text mining; OpenStreetMap; Google Trends and Books.
- [Did Detectorists Start a Boom?](https://maps.tristanhotham.com/detectorists-effect/): UK searches and Portable Antiquities Scheme finds, 2004 to 2026: did a sitcom send people out with metal detectors? DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23666467 Tags: Archaeology; Metal detecting; Film and television; Present day; UK; Before and after test; Portable Antiquities Scheme; Google Trends and Books.
